raw_response:
## Recommendation

Start with **TheirStack**, and compare it with **PredictLeads** on a small set of companies you already understand. They are the strongest documented matches I found for preparing consultancy sales conversations from company technology signals. **HG Insights** is a broader enterprise alternative. **Sumble** and **Enlyft** are worth follow-up, but my document access was not sufficient to verify them to the same standard.

The key distinction for this use case is the evidence behind each claim. A technology mentioned in a job advertisement can be a useful opening for a conversation, but it does not establish that the company currently deploys it throughout the organization. Treat a returned stack as a set of research leads, with dates and source context.

### 1. TheirStack — first choice for the stated emphasis

TheirStack's official guide explicitly covers CI/CD and security tools, including examples such as Okta, CrowdStrike, Splunk, and Vault. Its company-technographics endpoint returns confidence levels, job-mention counts, and first/last mention dates; its documented filters let you select confidence levels, categories, and recency. This makes it a practical first API to evaluate for your use case.

Sources: [internal-stack guide](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/guides/how-to-discover-tech-stack-of-any-company) and [API reference](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/api-reference/companies/technographics_v1).

I would begin with recent, higher-confidence signals and inspect the underlying context before phrasing a sales question as an established fact. The documented fit is strong; I have not tested its accuracy on your accounts.

### 2. PredictLeads — strongest alternative for inspecting detection evidence

PredictLeads documents a company technology-detections endpoint and an extended-detection endpoint. The latter exposes the clues behind a detection, including job, webpage, DNS, and connection evidence; the data model includes first/last seen dates and source counts. That is particularly useful when your previous failure was an unsupported stack assertion.

Source: [Technology Detections API and data model](https://docs.predictleads.com/v3/guide/technology_detections_dataset/api_endpoints).

Check the particular CI/CD and security products you care about in a sample. I verified the documented evidence workflow, not coverage or present deployment at any specific company.

### 3. HG Insights — broader enterprise alternative

HG documents technographic company enrichment by domain, with installation-related metadata. Its methodology article describes combining company-produced documents with digital signals and retaining verification dates. That is a plausible alternative when you need wider enterprise account intelligence.

Sources: [company enrichment API](https://data-docs.hginsights.com/v2/guides/enrichment) and [installation methodology](https://support.hginsights.com/articles/6696649277-introduction-to-technology-installs).

Ask for a sample containing the exact CI/CD and security tools and target companies relevant to your consultancy. The public documentation supports the API research workflow; it does not establish those specific coverage or purchasing details. Also, the [API overview](https://help.hginsights.com/docs/hg-api) was updated after the question date, so the current documentation should not be read as a complete record of what was available in July 2026.

### 4. Sumble — promising, with verification still needed

Official indexed documentation describes organization technology enrichment and job-based account evidence. However, the opened API and methodology pages exposed only documentation pointers in this run. I would retain Sumble as an evaluation option, conditional on confirming its endpoint schemas, evidence access, and coverage of your relevant technologies.

Sources: [API documentation](https://docs.sumble.com/api) and [data methodology](https://docs.sumble.com/our-data). These are preliminary leads from official search excerpts, not fully verified opened-body evidence.

### 5. Enlyft — another option to verify

Official search results identify a public API and a technology-lookup capability through its MCP documentation. The REST page returned no readable body, and the opened MCP excerpt only established setup/authentication. It therefore remains a follow-up candidate, rather than an equally verified recommendation.

Sources: [public API documentation](https://docs.enlyft.com/) and [MCP documentation](https://mcp.enlyft.com/docs).

## How I would choose

Run the same small account set through the leading candidates, using companies whose stack you can independently check. Evaluate useful CI/CD/security detections, source traceability, observation dates, company matching, and false positives. Include a few companies with little public hiring to expose coverage gaps. This is a proposed evaluation method, not a benchmark I performed.

For the eventual sales brief, retain the technology, observation date, source reference, and uncertainty. A question such as “I saw a recent role mentioning Jenkins; is that still part of your delivery setup?” uses the signal without turning inference into fact. You can then use an LLM to organize supplied evidence while requiring unsupported claims to remain unknown.

No explicit price, platform, license, or no-AI prohibition was present in the supplied summary, so I did not exclude products on those grounds. Prices and actual API results were not tested. Research used live public material on November 21, 2026; undated pages are marked unknown, and observed later revisions are marked post-decision. The original question thread and its answers were not used.
